title: Source registry — sources.json
description: Generated from SOURCES.md by `npm run data:sources` (I-04b). The machine-readable half of the registry: licence, verification, status and the attribution each licence requires. The Sources panel's prose is bilingual UI text and lives in assets/content/{lang}, keyed by the same ids — a licence registry cannot be translated, and translated prose cannot be the licence of record. Added in 1.4.0.

sources.description: Datasets the project may use. A status other than `ok` or `limited` must not reach published data — SOURCES.md's own rule (0-02, 0-03).

ref.description: DOI or URL as the registry records it.

verified.description: Where and when the licence was checked.

status.description: ok = verified and usable; limited = usable within a stated restriction; unresolved = licence unknown, publication forbidden; excluded = licence rules the planned use out.

attribution.description: Verbatim text the licence requires, where it requires one.

unused.description: Registered but not yet used anywhere in tools/ or src/. Status speaks about the licence, never about use.

citations.description: Publications whose numbers enter the contract — phase boundaries, sill elevations, lake levels. Facts are not copyrightable, so these carry a citation and no licence.

rejected.description: Ids kept on record as rejected, so a reader can see what was considered and why SOURCES.md says it was dropped.
